text: Imagine an 11-year-old child...
...who puts all his savings into his first share.
And within a few days, the share starts falling.
Out of fear, he sells it...
...at a small profit. Then he watches the same share...
...grow 5 times. That day, the child learned a lesson
that later made him the world's most famous *investor*.
His name was *Warren Buffett*.
In this series, we tell the complete story of Warren Buffett
in 3 parts: from birth to struggle,
and from struggle to becoming the *Oracle of Omaha*.
Before we start: if you like such motivational stories,
*subscribe* to the channel and press the *bell icon*
so you don't miss Part 2.
*30 August 1930.*
In Omaha, Nebraska, a small city in America, *Warren Edward Buffett* was born.
Now look at the timing. Just one year earlier,
in *1929*, America's stock market crashed.
The whole country fell into the *Great Depression*.
People were losing their jobs.
Banks were shutting down. The bank where Warren's father, Howard Buffett, worked also closed.
Money was tight at home.
But Howard didn't give up.
He started his own small *brokerage firm*.
And from here, little Warren saw money, hard work and risk up close.
While other kids played with toys,
Warren played with *numbers*.
At just 6, he bought a 6-pack of Coca-Cola from his grandfather's grocery store for *25 cents*.
He sold each bottle for *5 cents*.
So 6 bottles brought in 30 cents.
Profit: just *5 cents*.
You might say, what's 5 cents?
But that day, Warren understood:
*buy cheap, sell at value*, and keep adding up the profits.
This thinking later built a company worth *billions*.
At 11, Warren bought his *first share*.
3 shares of Cities Service,
at *$38* per share.
Soon, the share fell to *$27*.
Warren panicked. As soon as it came back to *$40*, he sold.
A small profit. And then...
...a few years later, the same share reached about *$200*.
Warren learned *two lessons* he remembered all his life.
First: don't get stuck on the price you paid.
Second: don't rush.
*Patience* is what makes real money.
Friends, if this lesson helped you, *like* this video and *share* it with the friend who panics quickly in the stock market.
In *1942*, Warren's father was elected to the US Congress,
and the whole family moved to Washington DC.
New city, new people.
Warren was not happy at all.
His grades dropped at school. He didn't feel like studying.
But he turned his unhappiness into one thing.
Every morning, he started delivering *newspapers*.
Hundreds of newspapers, every day.
At *13*, he filed his first *income tax return*,
and claimed his bicycle as a *business expense*.
In high school, Warren and a friend bought an old *pinball machine* for *$25*
and placed it in a barbershop.
Customers played while they waited,
and the money came in. 1 machine became 3,
then more than 3. Later, this business was sold for *$1,200*.
And with that money, at just 15,
Warren bought a *40-acre farm* in Nebraska.
A teenager who owned land.
Warren didn't want to go to college.
He thought: I'm already doing business,
why study? But at his father's insistence, he studied
and graduated at just *19*.
Then he applied to the world's most famous business school,
*Harvard Business School*.
He gave the interview... and Harvard *rejected* him.
Think about it: a boy who had been doing business since childhood
was turned down by the top school in the world.
He could have broken down. But this rejection became the *biggest turning point* of his life.
Because at that very time, he had a *book* in his hands,
and found a *guru* who changed his entire thinking.
That story is in *Part 2*.
Today's lesson: rejection is *not the end*.
Sometimes, it's the start of the *right path*.
If you have ever faced rejection,
write in the comments: *I won't stop*.
*Like* the video, *share* it with your friends,
and *subscribe* to the channel,
because Warren Buffett's real struggle begins in *Part 2*.
See you in the next part.
